transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-30
Start: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Mills (Blueleaf Head of ML), Priya Rao (Infra Lead), Diego Fernandez (CTO)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results versus Blueleaf's baseline provider. Discussed latency/throughput numbers, tuning levers (batching, quantization, KV cache), and next steps to run additional runs and share logs. Agreed to follow up with detailed CSV and schedule on-prem tests if needed.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thank you for joining, we'll give a quick recap then dive into the benchmark numbers ravi will walk the charts
[00:12] Jordan (Blueleaf): yeah thanks, excited to see where we landed after last week's changes
[00:18] Ravi (Redwood): cool quick note timeline — these are the runs we did on 7/28 and 7/29, mixed traffic profile, 1k and 4k contexts, 50% read heavy, 50% generate, and we compared against Blueleaf's baseline cluster on ProviderX
[00:36] Priya: just to confirm, baseline is 2x gpus per host with stock model container right?
[00:43] Jordan: yes baseline = ProviderX managed endpoints, default batching, quantization disabled in baseline
[00:50] Ravi: ok got it, so first slide — median latency (per token) for the rwd-7b-q4b quantized profile on Redwood Dedicated was 45ms median vs baseline 72ms median under same concurrency
[01:10] Diego: can you remind me what rwd-7b-q4b means? i think the name changed in prior notes
[01:16] Ravi: sorry yeah shorthand — our 7b model with 4-bit dynamic quantization profile, the one tuned for throughput in the POC. sometimes labels in the export got truncated so you might see rwd7b_q4
[01:30] Maya: quick callout p95 numbers are usually more important for your SLA, we'll surface both
[01:36] Ravi: right p95 with the same config was 210ms on Redwood vs 340ms on ProviderX — so roughly 35-40% improvement at p95 for that model and traffic mix
[01:52] Jordan: that's pretty promising. what's the throughput? tokens per second or requests per minute?
[01:58] Ravi: we reported both — for the 4k context case throughput at steady state was ~1.6k tokens/sec per GPU on Redwood Dedicated vs ~1.1k tokens/sec on baseline. request-level throughput (avg requests/sec for 128-token responses) was 220 rps vs 150 rps
[02:18] Priya: those numbers are for single-GPU equivalent or per-host?
[02:22] Ravi: per GPU. our Dedicated nodes in this run were configured with isolated GPUs, so scaling is linear-ish across nodes but we did single-GPU comparisons to be apples-to-apples
[02:32] Jordan: do you have the batch sizes used? I remember small batches helped latency but hurt throughput sometimes
[02:37] Ravi: yes for Redwood we auto-batched up to 64 tokens and configured a batching window of 8ms for that run; baseline used default provider batching of 20ms and larger batch cap so it collected bigger batches which helped throughput but increased p95
[02:56] Diego: can you explain where KV cache saved time in these numbers? we saw mixed results when we tried prefix caching on ProviderX
[03:03] Ravi: sure, KV cache reduced token generation cost when reusing previous contexts — in our run we saw ~12% token-level saving when cache hits were >30% of requests. ProviderX didn't have prefix-level cache enabled in their default config, so that partly explains gap
[03:20] Jordan: nice. any memory tradeoffs for the cache?
[03:23] Ravi: small memory overhead — per-request KV is kept per session, we evict LRU at the session cap, and it increased mem by roughly 6-8% in these runs. nothing that affected OOMs in our Dedicated test fleet
[03:35] Priya: about the quantization — did you test q4 vs q8? we want to check quality delta too
[03:41] Ravi: yes we ran q8 and dynamic q4 — q8 had slightly better generation quality on our eval set (BLEU-ish and human checks), but q4 reduced latency by ~20% vs q8. we included small eval samples in the sheet
[03:55] Jordan: we care about hallucination rates too; did quantization bump that?
[04:00] Ravi: minor uptick in hallucination for q4 on some prompt families — we flagged this in the notes and suggested mixed strategy: critical calls use q8, background tasks use q4
[04:12] Maya: that's a common tradeoff — we'll include split routing suggestions in the doc
[04:18] Diego: curious about cold-starts and tokenization overhead, baseline had worse cold-starts in our spikes
[04:24] Ravi: right Cold starts — we warm KV cache and keep hot workers for typical traffic in Dedicated; baseline had container spin-ups, we saw a few 2-3s cold-start outliers on ProviderX which pushed p99 up
[04:39] Priya: you mentioned p99 numbers earlier? can we get those?
[04:42] Ravi: p99 was 890ms on ProviderX vs 520ms on Redwood for the 4k case — there's still room for tuning but gap is meaningful
[04:54] Jordan: is that with autoscaling enabled? I worry scale up/down adds latency
[04:58] Ravi: these numbers are measured during steady-state after scale up; autoscale events did cause spikes — we collect that separately and we can show you cold-scale traces
[05:10] Maya: let's switch to throughput tuning we tried an aggressive batching run last night
[05:15] Ravi: yeah so last night's run used bigger batch caps 256 and batching window 40ms — that pushed token throughput to ~2.4k tokens/sec per GPU but median latency rose to 95ms and p95 to 410ms
[05:30] Jordan: so depending on target you can tune either for throughput or tight latency - we need to see where your traffic shape sits
[05:37] Diego: our traffic is spiky — baseline handled burst by queuing which increased p95 a lot. what's Redwood behavior under bursts?
[05:45] Ravi: Redwood offers burst capacity and also a priority queue. Under burst we keep low-latency lanes for small requests and let large batches go to throughput lane — this reduces p95 for critical paths. we can show config examples
[05:58] Priya: what about network egress or infra overhead? provider had noisy neighbors causing variability
[06:04] Ravi: in Dedicated we isolate physical GPUs and tune NUMA and kernel settings; our variance was lower in runs — CoV for latency was 0.12 vs ProviderX 0.2 in same runs
[06:18] Jordan: do you have the raw CSVs? we want to plug into our dashboards
[06:22] Ravi: yes i'll share raw CSV and the summarized sheet after the call — includes per-request timestamped latencies and config used per run
[06:30] Maya: quick question from Diego — what about private/VPC deployment if we decide to test on-prem later?
[06:36] Ravi: we can export the same workload runner — for Private deployment you can replicate the Dedicated config; performance will vary by your HW but we can help tune kernels and compilation flags
[06:46] Diego: awesome. any compliance impacts on metrics collection? we need to avoid PII in logs
[06:51] Maya: we redact payloads by default in our POC logs, and we can provide an audit-friendly export. we also have KMS integration for keys and SOC2 docs if needed
[07:02] Jordan: good. quick nit — some of the label names in the spreadsheet looked truncated, could you normalize the model names?
[07:08] Ravi: noted — we'll normalize column names and include a legend in the CSV
[07:12] Priya: what's the best config to try next week? we have limited time for runs
[07:17] Ravi: recommend two focused runs: (1) production-like latency SLO run — batching window 8ms, q4 dynamic but pinned for critical route, KV cache on; (2) throughput run — batch cap 256, window 40ms, q8 for quality, no cache. that'll highlight the tradeoffs
[07:36] Jordan: sounds good. can you estimate cost delta vs baseline for those configs? we care about ops cost not just perf
[07:42] Ravi: we ran rough unit economics — tokens/sec per GPU increased so unit cost fell approx 18% for q4-latency tuned run vs baseline. throughput-tuned run had 28% lower unit cost but higher latency. we'll include per-token cost table in the CSV
[07:59] Diego: do you have any logs that show memory pressure or OOMs during big batches? we hit an OOM once on baseline last week
[08:06] Ravi: we monitored OOMs — none in our Dedicated fleet for these runs. biggest memory spike was during 4k context with large batch caps, but node memory stayed within 85% usage
[08:20] Priya: regarding security review, Jordan asked for network diagrams — can you attach the VPC peering example for Private deployment?
[08:27] Maya: yes i'll include the VPC peering diagram, KMS notes, and our SOC2 brief in the follow-up packet
[08:34] Jordan: perfect. some of our ML folks wanted to test reranking workload later — do you support embedding compute on the same nodes?
[08:42] Ravi: embeddings can run on separate lower-memory instances or on same nodes if you reserve memory; for POC we used separate embedding workers to avoid competing for GPU memory
[08:52] Diego: what's the recommended GPU type? we currently have A100s but some of our infra folks prefer H100s for perf
[08:58] Ravi: H100s gives better kernel-level perf for certain attention patterns; A100 is solid and what we used for these runs. if you migrate to H100 you'll likely see further latency and throughput improvements but we should re-run kernels selection
[09:12] Maya: quick check-in — are we aligned on next steps? Ravi will share CSVs and normalized model names, Maya sends compliance pack, Jordan provides traffic shape and p95 target
[09:22] Jordan: correct. also we'll confirm if we want to run Private on-prem test week of 8/11
[09:28] Priya: one more question on failover — if a node goes down how do you fallback to baseline or hosted?
[09:34] Ravi: we have routing policies — you can set automatic fallback to Hosted Redwood API or to a smaller compatible model on Dedicated; failovers are async and we expose metrics for rollback decisions
[09:47] Diego: that's useful. last question: can you include artifact links in the CSV? the sheet we saw referenced a trace link but it was truncated
[09:54] Ravi: yes links will be full URLs in the raw CSV and we'll attach gzipped logs separately because of size
[10:00] Maya: ok let's do a quick recap and owners
[10:03] Jordan: go ahead
[10:04] Maya: recap — action items and due dates captured, we'll follow up with files by EOD tomorrow. any objections?
[10:12] Jordan: none from me
[10:14] Priya: all good
[10:15] Diego: good to move forward
[10:17] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll circle up next week same time unless we need an ad hoc on-prem planning call
[10:24] Jordan: thanks all
[10:26] Meeting end
